title: Development of the Sexual Experiences Survey-Victimization-Short Forms (SES-V-SF) and a Psychometric Evaluation of SES-V Standard and Short Forms.
abstract: The Sexual Experiences Survey-Victimization (SES-V) was substantially revised in 2024 to broaden the range of sexual exploitation victimization assessed. Although the revised SES-V offers important advantages, its length may limit its usefulness in some research and applied contexts. The purpose of this study was to develop a short form of the SES-V and to evaluate the psychometric performance of both the short-form and the standard-form SES-V. Using a predefined process, we selected two to four items from each SES-V module. These items captured 89% to 96% of the victimization reported within each module in a national dataset. We then recruited 1,103 adults through CloudResearch, oversampling groups previously underrepresented in SES-V research. Participants were randomized to complete the standard-form SES-V or one of two short-form versions along with measures to assess convergent validity. A subsample of participants ( = 640) completed the same SES-V form again two weeks later to assess test-retest reliability. The short forms performed well and were comparable to the standard form in convergent validity and test-retest reliability. Endorsement rates on the short forms were similar to the standard form across three of four modules, and the short forms required less than half the administration time (i.e. a median of under five minutes). Findings were generally consistent across demographic subgroups. This study provides psychometric support for the short forms and additional psychometric evidence for the standard form. Future research should further examine whether the short forms capture the full range of victimization across diverse populations.
